_note: The scenario pack. `dev/scripts/viz/build.py` runs each `argv` verbatim and refuses
to publish a page whose run stopped matching the `expect_*` fields. That is the
whole point of the file: a pinned seed is only meaningful as (commit, seed, flags),
so every claim a narration makes out loud is pinned here and machine-checked on
every build. A scenario that quietly changes behaviour fails the build instead of
shipping a stale claim (the failure commit 1e80be3 already fixed once).
What is pinned is the STORY, not the weather: the exit code, which oracle fired and
with what text, which oracles held and which never executed, the ack split, the
objects left at quiescence, a graph's node and edge counts. Storage-op and
trace-event totals are NOT pinned and narrations do not quote them — they move by a
handful on any commit that touches the replication path, no reader's conclusion
changes when 1,166 becomes 1,165, and pinning them meant a product change reddened
`make viz` for something that was never a finding. The page renders both totals live
from the trace it is playing, so they are always right; `build.py` prints them as an
observation and refuses a scenario that tries to pin them again.
Every vopr `argv` carries `--recheck-every 0`, and it is load-bearing rather than
tidy. The determinism recheck re-executes a seed whenever `seed % --recheck-every`
is 0 (default 10), and the two executions are not symmetric on the page: the trace
brackets ONE of them, while the terminal's reach table is process-cumulative and
counts BOTH. A reader who pasted the command a page printed therefore saw every
oracle count and every merge-evidence count at exactly twice the page's figure.
Disabling the recheck makes the traced run the only execution, so page and terminal agree
number for number. The `determinism` scenario is the deliberate exception — it sets
`--recheck-every 1` because the double execution is its subject — and it carries a
caveat saying so.
status: live      built and verified on every run
retired   a finding that has been adjudicated away; not run, shown as closed
pending   its producer does not exist yet; build.py fails once `needs` appears
may_skip             the named local dependency may be absent, and then the page is not
built and says so on the index instead of failing the build
expect_event_kinds   event types that must all appear, or the recording measures nothing
expect_exit          the process exit code (0 clean, 2 invariant violation, 3 determinism, 4 reach gate)
expect_violation     null for a clean run; otherwise a substring, or a LIST of substrings when
the run reds more than once. Every violation printed must match one entry
and every entry must be matched, so a new violation cannot slip in quietly
expect_event_counts  per-event-type line counts in the JSONL. `op` is refused here on purpose
(incidental); `oracle`, `violation` and `round` are the ones worth pinning
expect_log           substrings the run's own terminal output must still contain — for a claim
the recording cannot carry because the producer prints it (`--shrink`)
expect_acks          the ack split, because `acks` is three numbers: `answered` (every upload
and delete the workload issued), `accepted`/`refused` (whether the server
took it), and `distinct_files_acked` (filenames the ledger holds an
accepted upload for — the `N acked` verdict pill on the page)
expect_world         objects left at quiescence, folded from the `world` deltas by build.py.
`quarantine` counts OBJECTS, `distinct_quarantined_bodies` counts
BYTE-SETS; a narration saying `preserved bodies` means the second
expect_oracles       per-oracle `verdict` the page must render: `held`, `violated` or
`not-executed`, keyed by the REACH_METER label
expect_counts        graph producers only: keys read straight out of the payload's `counts`

scenarios.title: One filename, two bodies, three regions
scenarios.narration: Two writers publish different bytes under the same immutable filename in three regions. When the dust settles the filename is frozen in all three, and both byte-sets are still on disk — two distinct bodies, kept as four _quarantine/ copies across the three regions. The fleet refuses to pick a winner and refuses to lose one: CONVERGENCE and FREEZE_JUSTIFIED both hold.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

Byte identity here is per key: the three buckets agree on truth and views, and deliberately do not agree on their own bucket-local state (`_state/`, `.origin` stamps) or on which quarantined copies they hold.

scenarios.title: The smallest world that can conflict
scenarios.narration: Two nodes, two regions, one filename, sixteen workload ops — the smallest world in this pack that can conflict at all. The contested name ends fenced with .frozen on both sides and the losing body is kept under _quarantine/ rather than overwritten.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.
Which merge verdicts a seed presents is not pinned here — only the evidence left at quiescence is. The fence and the preserved body are the claim; the route to them is the simulator's business.

scenarios.title: Same seed, writes pinned to one region: the merge algebra never runs
scenarios.narration: Three nodes, two regions, every write homed to the same region: four uploads accepted over four distinct filenames with nothing refused, and not one .frozen fence or _quarantine/ body is ever created. The merge algebra is compiled in, wired up, and never asked a question — the two oracles that judge it render "not executed".
caveats: This is the control run. Its partner `dead-code-partitioned` is the same seed and the same topology with one flag added; the player plays the two side by side and does not diff them.

scenarios.title: Same seed. One flag. The merge algebra wakes up
scenarios.narration: Add --partition 100 and nothing else: the same seed now leaves four .frozen fences and four preserved bodies — held as five _quarantine/ copies, one of them a second region's copy of a body another region also kept — where the aligned run left none. Same code, same seed; the flag decides whether the merge algebra is ever handed a question, and here both oracles that judge it execute and hold.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

The chip row's two op numbers are read live off this trace and they are not the same measurement: `storage ops traced` counts the gated storage calls, `hashed trace events` is what the determinism hash covers — the same calls plus one record per compare-and-set outcome, so it is the larger of the two. The binary's own summary line prints the second figure, under the name `storage-op interleavings`. Neither is pinned in the pack: both move with the product and neither changes what this page shows.
The aligned twin is a separate run of the same seed. Two panels, one clock, no diff engine.

scenarios.title: The multi-region nightly profile, one seed
scenarios.narration: The nightly's multi-region profile plus --partition 100 on a single seed: 22 client requests answered, of which 11 were accepted (10 uploads over 8 distinct filenames — the 8 the verdict pill counts — and one delete) and 11 were deletes the server refused; six .frozen fences; six preserved bodies held as seven _quarantine/ copies; and all twelve oracles that executed held. The other eleven slots never ran, and the page says which — an oracle nobody watched is not evidence.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

This is the one page in the pack that pins all 23 oracle verdicts, because "every oracle that executed held" is its whole claim: an oracle that silently stopped executing, or one that started, fails the build here.

The chip row's two op numbers are read live off this trace and they are not the same measurement: `storage ops traced` counts the gated storage calls, `hashed trace events` is what the determinism hash covers — the same calls plus one record per compare-and-set outcome, which is why the command above reports the larger figure under the name `storage-op interleavings`.
One seed is a sample, not the nightly. The per-oracle execution counts on this page are this seed's own; the nightly's are in dev/TESTING.md.

scenarios.title: Run the same seed twice and compare everything
scenarios.narration: Every other page on this index is a pinned seed, which is only evidence if it replays. Here that is the subject: --recheck-every 1 re-executes seed 21 from nothing once the first run finishes and compares the whole storage-op sequence and the final world hash against it — every storage op in the same order, the same two .frozen fences, the same three preserved bodies. The DETERMINISM oracle is the one asserting it, and it holds.
caveats: This is the one page in the pack whose printed command runs the seed TWICE, so read the two side by side with care: every count on this page is ONE execution, while the terminal's reach table and merge-evidence table are process-cumulative and cover BOTH. The command reports DURABILITY 4 where the page reads 2, and six `_quarantine/<pkg>/<file>@sha` objects where the page's world holds three. DETERMINISM is the exception in the other direction — it fires once per seed, so it reads 1 in both. Every other vopr page in this pack passes `--recheck-every 0`, which disables the recheck entirely and makes page and terminal agree number for number.

The chip row's two op numbers are read live off this trace and they are not the same measurement: `storage ops traced` counts the gated storage calls, `hashed trace events` is what the determinism hash covers — the same calls plus one record per compare-and-set outcome. The binary's own summary line prints the second figure, under the name `storage-op interleavings`.

What the oracle compares is the op trace and a hash of the final world, not the recording: the second execution is not traced. A nondeterminism that produced identical calls and identical final bytes by a different internal route would pass.
`--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

scenarios.title: A download a client would reject, and everything else green
scenarios.narration: We repoint one sidecar at a digest no stored body has, and of the 23 oracle slots exactly one fires — SELF_CONSISTENCY, which is the check a real client performs when it hashes the file it was handed against the index it read.
caveats: The defect is injected by `--break attest`, not produced by the product. This is a mutation test proving the oracle can fire — not a bug found in the wild.
One bucket, so the cross-region oracles (CONVERGENCE, ACK_TOTALITY) do not execute on this run and render as "not executed".

scenarios.title: The fleet never agrees, and the clock says by how much
scenarios.narration: We park one _repl/ object no sweep recognizes, so no fixpoint exists — and the run reds on a clock, not on a retry budget. 21,000 seconds of simulated time after the last write, one record is still outstanding against the 390s this fleet had earned: 300s of healthy promise plus one 90s convergence cycle for the 22 records of replication debt it was holding when the storm ended. Only then does the second violation land, the one that says the heal loop exhausted all twelve rounds without ever standing still.
expect_violation: STALENESS: the fleet never agreed — 21000s of simulated time after the last write and 1 record(s) still outstanding, against a 390s deadline (300s healthy + 1 cycle(s) x 90s for the 22 record(s) of replication debt it held when the storm ended)
STALENESS: the fleet never stopped working — no fixpoint in 12 heal rounds x 20 drain passes (21000s of simulated time); leftover markers: ["bucket0:_repl/vopr-wedge"]
caveats: The defect is injected by `--break wedge`, not produced by the product. This is a mutation test proving the oracle can fire — not a bug found in the wild.

This page used to red on LIVENESS, which asked only for a fixpoint inside HEAL_ROUNDS x DRAIN_PASSES. Those two bounds are made up, and a fleet that converged on round 11 was the same green as one that converged on round 1. STALENESS replaced it (76334ff): the deadline is a time the fleet's own debt buys it, so the failure now names how late it is and against what. The loop bounds survive only as loop bounds — a run that hits one has already blown the time bound, which is why both violations fire here and the time one fires first.
A green run of this profile settles in the first rounds of the twelve; the tightest seed on record peaked at 2 of 12 heal rounds and 1 of 20 drain passes (dev/TESTING.md:1596).

scenarios.title: It converged. Ninety seconds too late
scenarios.narration: The hardest kind of bug to see: nothing is lost, nothing diverges, every other oracle holds — the fleet is merely slow. A peer's copy of a live record is stolen the instant convergence finishes, leaving no breadcrumb over the loss, so only the pairwise tree diff will find it: one more whole cycle of simulated time. 480s to agree after the last write, against the 390s its debt had bought it. CONVERGENCE holds, DURABILITY holds, CONSERVATION holds, the world at quiescence is intact, and the run still fails — because "we agree eventually" was never the promise.
scenarios.expect_violation: STALENESS: the fleet took 480s of simulated time to agree after the last write, past its 390s deadline (300s healthy + 1 cycle(s) x 90s for the 75 record(s) of replication debt it held when the storm ended)
caveats: The defect is injected by `--break slow-repair`, not produced by the product. This is a mutation test proving the oracle can fire — not a bug found in the wild.

It is the kill proof STALENESS needed and LIVENESS could not have. LIVENESS asked only whether a fixpoint was reached, and a fixpoint reached late is still a fixpoint, so this break is invisible to it by construction — not by measurement; `--break slow-repair` did not exist while LIVENESS did. The 0-of-500-seeds figure on record belongs to the other bug: against a clock latched on the FIRST agreement, this break shipped dead, killing 0 of 500 while doing real extra repair work the clock could not see (examples/vopr.rs:1105-1113). Latching on the LAST moment the fleet agreed (6a688d5) is what made it killable.

The deadline is affine in the debt sampled when the storm ended, never in live debt: a fleet that keeps re-creating work it failed to consume must not be able to buy itself more time. See the STALENESS header block in examples/vopr.rs.

scenarios.title: The same bug, in five workload ops instead of eighty
scenarios.narration: This is `catch-it` after the shrinker ran: one node, one bucket, one package, one filename, five publishes, no injected faults — and the identical SELF_CONSISTENCY violation. `--shrink` found it by descending the profile dimensions on the same seed, keeping any smaller world that still fails THE SAME WAY, to a fixpoint. The command this page prints IS the answer, and it is a fixpoint: the run re-shrinks itself and comes back with the same command, byte for byte. Detection was never the bottleneck — the soak fleet finds these unattended. Reading `catch-it`'s 717-op trace by hand was.
caveats: The defect is injected by `--break attest`, not produced by the product. This is a mutation test proving the oracle can fire — not a bug found in the wild.

The pack pins the shrinker's ANSWER, not its search: `expect_log` requires this run's own `shrunk:` line to be the command above, which is what makes it a proven fixpoint rather than a claim. Reaching it from `catch-it`'s eighty ops takes a few dozen simulations and a few milliseconds — a property of the search path, deliberately not pinned. dev/TESTING.md:1052 carries the measured seed budget for all 23 kill proofs.

`--shrink` prints its report instead of the run's usual reach and merge-evidence tables and stops at the first failing seed: a shrink is a diagnosis session, not a sample. The extra simulations it runs to prove minimality are not traced, so the recording on this page is the one run named by the command — nothing on screen is a shrink probe.

The reduced world is a different world, so the byte that fails is not the same object `catch-it` shows: same oracle, same defect, one filename instead of four. Op-SEQUENCE shrinking is deliberately absent — a skipped op is not expressible as a profile and would shift every fault after it — so five ops is the floor these axes can reach, not a proof that four cannot fail.

scenarios.title: The freeze nobody could justify
scenarios.narration: Seed 1327 froze a filename fleet-wide with only one byte-set attested for it — the last open finding with a millisecond repro, closed at 439b839.
scenarios.retired_because: Adjudicated: `fix: a freeze whose evidence a racing delete erased read as unjustified` (439b839). The seed now exits 0 and prints FREEZE_JUSTIFIED. It was an oracle bug, not a product bug, so there is nothing left to show — and a page that still called it open would be exactly the stale evidence this pack exists to prevent.

scenarios.title: Every interleaving of two writers racing one filename
scenarios.narration: The exhaustive state space of two private uploads of the same immutable filename into different regions — 80 states, 178 transitions, 99 of them joins where independent orders reconverge on the same world.

scenarios.title: The _dirty/ marker protocol, drawn in full at a reduced size
scenarios.narration: Every interleaving of one upload, one delete and one worker tick over the _dirty/ intent-and-commit markers — 758 states, 1,455 transitions — beside the 1,497,544-state configuration CI checks on every merge and nobody can draw.

scenarios.title: The region a node reads from goes dark
scenarios.narration: Reads fall back to the write region in seconds, the write pin never moves, a real uv pip install keeps working, and reads return only once that region is healthy and owes nothing.

scenarios.title: The preferred region goes dark; reads stay in their region
scenarios.narration: The fleet-wide write home goes dark while this node reads from a different region: new writes move to the next healthy region in preference order and the node's reads never leave home.

scenarios.title: How much of this has actually been run
scenarios.narration: Every figure on this page carries the file and line it was measured at — and the commit, wherever the source records one; the build refuses to publish a figure without a source. The two live rows are re-measured on this machine at build time.
